sections.overview: The Japanese wobbegong is a small, nocturnal carpet shark of the northwestern and west-central Pacific.
sections.identification: It reaches about 118 cm total length and has a flattened body, mottled camouflage and fleshy lobes around the mouth.
sections.habitat: It lives on the continental shelf, from the intertidal zone to about 200 m, especially on rocky and coral reefs.
sections.diet: It feeds on fishes and bottom-dwelling invertebrates, including crustaceans and cephalopods.
sections.behavior: By day it can remain concealed on the seabed; its nocturnal habits and reef shelter may reduce encounters with fisheries.
sections.reproduction: It is viviparous; the IUCN account reports litters of 20–27 and a gestation of about 12 months.
sections.ecology: Unlike the Australian Orectolobus profiles here, this species ranges from Japan to Vietnam; local records in Taiwan can be confused with O. leptolineatus.
sections.conservation: The 2020 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, while noting possible local fishing-related declines and limited population data.
